findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow lifecycle has no enum-based typestate; callers can construct any combination of status/is_validated/is_sent arbitrarily, including states the workflow should never reach.
findings.failure_mode: A caller sets status="sent" but leaves is_validated=false and is_sent=false (or sets is_validated=false after mark_sent), representing an invalid lease state that the domain logic cannot detect or prevent.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single LeaseState enum (e.g., LeaseState { Draft, Validated { validated_at: u64 }, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }) whose variants own all lifecycle data and make illegal states unrepresentable.

findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value; mark_sent hardcodes "sent" as a magic string literal on line 10.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set status to any value ("sent", "SENT", "pending", "", null bytes, etc.) bypassing the intended state machine. The magic string "sent" on line 10 is fragile and cannot be matched exhaustively by the compiler.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a `LeaseStatus` enum. mark_sent should construct the appropriate enum variant rather than assigning a string literal.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can be in invalid combinations (e.g., is_sent=true with is_validated=false).
findings.failure_mode: The workflow can enter a state where a lease is marked sent but never validated, or validated but sent from the wrong origin. These invalid combinations are undetectable at compile time and require runtime invariant checks scattered across all callers.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a typestate enum that encodes valid transitions. The enum variants should own all lifecycle data (e.g., sent_at_epoch_ms belongs in the Sent variant, not as a separate Option field).

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is decoupled from the lifecycle booleans; sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some without is_sent=true, and is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None.
findings.failure_mode: A lease can have sent_at_epoch_ms set but is_sent=false (ghost data), or is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None (missing required timestamp). The Option type does not enforce that the timestamp only exists when the lease is actually sent.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of the typestate enum: `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }` — making the timestamp mandatory only when the lease is sent, and impossible when it is not.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive; any caller can construct a LeaseWorkflow with an empty, malformed, or otherwise invalid id without domain-level validation.
findings.failure_mode: LeaseWorkflow can be constructed with id="" or id="   " or non-UUID/non-numeric strings, leading to silent data quality issues. The domain has no enforcement of id format or non-emptiness.
findings.fix: Replace `id: String` with a newtype `LeaseId(String)` created via a smart constructor that validates the id at construction (e.g., `LeaseId::new(s: &str) -> Result<LeaseId, ParseError>`). All domain APIs consume LeaseId, not String.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String for id, String for status, bool for flags, Option<u64> for timestamps) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors. Callers can construct invalid domain states directly from unvalidated inputs.
findings.failure_mode: Hostile or malformed inputs reach the core logic unchecked. There is no parse boundary — no smart constructors, no validation at construction, no typed errors for invalid inputs. Every field is directly settable by any caller.
findings.fix: Define fallible smart constructors for all domain types. LeaseWorkflow (or its typestate enum) should only be constructible through validated constructors that return Result<T, ParseError>. Raw primitives are parsed once at the shell boundary into trusted domain values.

findings.problem: mark_sent transitions any LeaseWorkflow to sent state without checking is_validated, allowing unvalidated leases to be marked sent.
findings.failure_mode: A LeaseWorkflow with is_validated=false can be marked sent, violating the domain invariant that only validated leases may be sent. The function has no preconditions or guards.
findings.fix: Either remove mark_sent entirely and require construction through a validated Sent variant of the typestate enum, or add a precondition check: if !item.is_validated { return Err(LeaseError::NotValidated) }. With a proper typestate enum, this check becomes a compile-time guarantee.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for this crate. The mark_sent function allocates via .to_string() on line 10.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation patterns are unmeasured. If mark_sent is called in a hot path, the String allocation on every call could cause performance regression or unbounded allocation in mission-critical contexts.
findings.fix: With a typestate enum, mark_sent becomes a pure state transition with zero allocations (no String allocation needed). Add a benchmark to prove the allocation budget for the hot path.

residual_risk: The crate has fundamental architectural violations: status as String, independent lifecycle booleans, decoupled Option fields, raw String ID, and missing parse boundary. These are BLOCKER-level issues that make illegal states representable. No commands were executed; the review is static-only. The crate cannot be delivered until typestate refactoring is completed and all absolute laws pass strict lint gates.
